# Results — Study 784 (Analyst-Cluster)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**fade NVDA after a same-week cluster of analyst upgrades** (short it, expecting the
sell-side pile-in to mark a top). Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month). Fingerprint `31db942be633` (NVDA + SPY, one combined panel,
adjusted/total-return daily closes).*

> **LABELLED PROXY.** The "cluster of analyst upgrades" dates are **not** a live analyst
> feed. They are a clearly-labelled proxy: **NVDA's real quarterly earnings weeks** — the
> canonical trigger of a same-week price-target-hike wave. The earnings dates are real,
> publicly-verifiable, and known ~3-4 weeks ahead (zero look-ahead). The honest cost of the
> proxy: it inherits **post-earnings-announcement drift** as a confound, reported below.

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `NVDA` (NVIDIA) + `SPY` (S&P 500), one combined panel: 2,889 rows, 2015-01-02 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **LABELLED PROXY**: 39 cluster anchors = NVDA earnings weeks 2016-Feb → 2025-Aug (real dates, 8-K / earnings-history archives) |
| Events resolvable | all **39** of 39 clusters have NVDA+SPY coverage around the anchor |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the abnormal return (NVDA − SPY) across 39 independent, non-overlapping cluster events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut; leave-one-out jackknife |
| Execution / costs | **calendar-known, zero look-ahead**: the earnings date is announced ~3-4 weeks ahead. Run-up = [anchor−K → anchor]; fade = [anchor → anchor+K]; net of 2× one-way cost × NAV. Gross AND net reported |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) for both legs |

**Selection & beta, named:** this is *one hand-picked mega-winner*. NVDA rose ~300× over the
sample, so its abnormal-vs-SPY return is positive on almost *any* window — the placebo
confirms even **random** 2-week NVDA windows beat SPY by **+2.0%** on average. Every "cluster"
number below must be read against that +2.0% single-name baseline, not against zero.

## The run-up — abnormal return, K sessions BEFORE the cluster (NVDA − SPY)

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up (k=10) | 39 | **+2.292%** | **+2.339** | 26/39 = 66.7% [51.0%, 79.4%] |
| 1-month run-up (k=21) | 39 | **+5.274%** | **+3.562** | 30/39 = 76.9% [61.7%, 87.4%] |

NVDA does run *up* into the cluster/earnings week — but at +2.3%/2wk it is barely above the
+2.0% baseline that *any* random 2-week NVDA window clears. The 1-month run-up (+5.3%) is more
than baseline drift, consistent with pre-earnings positioning on a hot name.

## The fade — abnormal return, K sessions AFTER the cluster (the tested short)

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week fade (k=10) | 39 | **+4.756%** | **+2.126** | 23/39 = 59.0% [43.4%, 72.9%] |
| 1-month fade (k=21) | 39 | **+5.060%** | **+1.964** | 23/39 = 59.0% [43.4%, 72.9%] |

**The fade thesis is dead — and wrong-signed.** After the cluster NVDA does not sag; it
**drifts up**, +4.76% in the next two weeks (*t* = +2.13) and +5.06% over the month. A
contrarian who *shorted* the cluster would have lost ~+4.8% of abnormal return per event, 39
times. This is textbook post-earnings-announcement drift / recommendation-change drift
(Bernard-Thomas; Gleason-Lee) surfacing on the exact window the folklore says to short.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event)

| cut | tail | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up | right | +2.292% | +2.003% (1.243%) | 0.408 |
| 2-week fade | left | +4.756% | +2.003% (1.243%) | 0.985 |

The run-up sits **dead-centre** of NVDA's own luck cloud (right-tail p = 0.41) — i.e. the
pre-cluster run-up is *indistinguishable* from an ordinary NVDA fortnight. The post-cluster
window, by contrast, sits in the far **right** tail (left-tail p = 0.985 ⇒ only ~1.5% of
random NVDA windows were this *positive*): the post-cluster drift is real and *upward* — the
exact opposite of the fade the study set out to test.

## Jackknife (leave-one-out) — 2-week fade *t*

Full-sample *t* = **+2.126**; across all 39 leave-one-out draws the *t* stays in
**[+1.838, +2.464]** — the upward post-cluster drift is broad, not one AI-boom quarter.

## Tradability — net of costs (calendar-known entry, zero look-ahead)

| window | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week fade | +4.756% (*t* +2.13) | +4.656% (*t* +2.08) | +4.556% (*t* +2.04) |
| 2-week run-up | +2.292% (*t* +2.34) | +2.192% (*t* +2.24) | +2.092% (*t* +2.13) |

The *fade* (the tested trade) is a **loser** at every cost level — you'd be shorting a
+4.7%/2wk window. The mirror-image *long-the-drift* survives costs, but it is (a) plain PEAD,
not novel, (b) measured on a single, extreme, hand-picked winner, and (c) sitting on top of
NVDA's +2%/fortnight baseline — none of which is a generalizable, capacity-bearing edge.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (bump = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = −0.02 (sd 1.30); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **3/20** seeds —
  a near-nominal small-sample false-positive rate at n = 39, so the detector is honest.
- **Planted run-up +1.0% (seed 803):** mean AR +0.78%, *t* = **+1.00**.
- **Planted run-up +2.0% (seed 803):** mean AR +1.78%, *t* = **+2.30** — a real bump is
  recovered monotonically.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **Weak** | The tested "fade" is **not real** — it is confidently *wrong-signed*: NVDA drifts **up** +4.76%/2wk (*t* = +2.13, placebo far-right p ≈ 0.985, jackknife-stable [+1.84, +2.46]) after the cluster, not down. What is genuinely present is an *upward* post-cluster drift — but it is textbook PEAD / recommendation drift measured on a single hand-picked mega-winner whose *random* windows already beat SPY by +2%, so it is neither novel nor the effect the folklore claims. Real-but-confounded and opposite-signed, not a real fade. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Mirage** | Nothing to bank *as a fade* — the fade loses ~+4.7%/event before you even pay to short one of the most expensive-to-borrow, most-crowded names on the tape. The mirror long-the-drift survives gross+net but is one-name PEAD on top of a +2% selection baseline: no capacity story, no cross-sectional edge, not a strategy. |

**In one sentence:** the "fade the analyst-upgrade cluster" trade is busted twice over on
NVDA — the stock *drifts up* after the cluster (+4.8%/2wk, *t* = +2.1), so fading it loses
money, and the only real effect in the data is a hand-picked, single-name post-earnings drift
that is neither the claim nor a generalizable edge.
